claims.source: NICAP, 'UFOs Intrude Into SAC Base Weapons Areas', quoting the CINCNORAD message of 11 November 1975, http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The message's opening, as excerpted: 'Since 28 Oct 75 numerous reports of suspicious objects have been received at the NORAD CU; reliable military personnel at Loring AFB, Maine, Wurtsmith AFB, Michigan, Malmstrom AFB, Mt, Minot AFB, ND, and Canadian Forces Station, Falconbridge, Ontario, Canada have visually sighted suspicious objects.'

The message also records a Malmstrom report the 24th NORAD Region log corroborates in kind: 'Malmstrom Montana report an object which sounded like a jet aircraft. FAA advised there were no jet aircraft in the vicinity.'

A NORAD press release of 13 November 1975 from Sudbury, Ontario records that two F-106 aircraft of the Air National Guard's 171st Fighter Interceptor Squadron at Selfridge ANGB, Michigan were scrambled in connection with the Falconbridge reports. Lt Col Brian Wooding, Control Centre Director at North Bay, and Capt. Gordon Hilchie, Director of Public Affairs for the 22nd NORAD Region, are named.

conflicts: It names Minot AFB where the 24th NORAD Region's own Senior Director's Log of 10 November 1975 names Minot Air Force Station, a radar site. Nothing opened by this board resolves which installation the sequence means.

desc: THE MESSAGE THAT TIES THE 1975 SEQUENCE TOGETHER IN THE COMMAND'S OWN VOICE. On 11 November 1975 the Commander-in-Chief of North American Air Defense Command sent a four-part message to NORAD units summarising the events of the preceding fortnight. Its opening is the single most quoted sentence in the 1975 material and it is worth quoting in full because of the adjective it uses about its own witnesses. The message names five installations across two countries and, unlike the Loring traffic, it does not call the objects helicopters. It calls them suspicious objects, and it says its sources were reliable military personnel. It also names Minot AFB, where the 24th NORAD Region's own log nine days earlier had named Minot Air Force Station, which is the one internal inconsistency in the 1975 record that this board has found and cannot resolve.
label: CINCNORAD four-part message, 11 November 1975
